summary: H.R. 10869, titled the 'Protect Clean Water Act', amends the Safe Drinking Water Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to provide increased and new funding for states to address emerging contaminants, specifically focusing on perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

affected_groups.effect: Guaranteed at least 25 percent of the newly authorized water pollution control grant funding for emerging contaminants.
affected_groups.group: Small and disadvantaged communities and treatment works serving fewer than 25,000 persons

affected_groups.effect: Receive allotted capitalization grants and oversee the distribution of funds for addressing emerging contaminants like PFAS.
affected_groups.group: State governments and loan fund administrators

key_provisions: Amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to increase the authorized funding level for the emerging contaminants state revolving fund program from $100,000,000 to $1,000,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to establish a new emerging contaminants grant program funded at $1,000,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2031.

Requires that at least 25 percent of the funds in the new water pollution control program be used for small and disadvantaged communities or entities operating treatment works serving fewer than 25,000 persons.
Prohibits funds deposited into the water pollution control revolving fund under the new section from being used to back tax-exempt bonds or obligations.
Directs states to select grant recipients based on established state priority determinations for project categories.
missing_information: Specific criteria for how states must allocate the remaining 75 percent of the water pollution control funds beyond existing priority systems.
Exact details on how capitalization grants will be distributed among individual states.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10869, titled the 'Protect Clean Water Act', amends the Safe Drinking Water Act and the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to provide increased and new funding for states to address emerging contaminants, specifically focusing on perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).
summary_detail.significance: The bill authorizes significant federal funding of $1 billion annually from fiscal year 2027 through 2031 for both drinking water and water pollution control programs targeting emerging contaminants, with specific carve-outs for small and disadvantaged communities.
